title: Affogato
summary: A scoop of quick vanilla ice cream 'drowned' in a shot of hot espresso at the table.
steps: Heat the cream until steaming. Whisk the yolks, allulose and salt, then slowly whisk in the hot cream.
Return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spatula and reaches 80 °C (176 °F). Strain, stir in the vanilla and chill until cold.
Churn in an ice-cream maker, or pour into a shallow container and freeze, stirring hard every 30 minutes for 3 hours. Freeze until firm.
To serve, put a firm scoop into each of four small, chilled cups and pour a hot espresso over it at the table.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut ice cream melts faster under hot coffee and gives a creamier, coconut-flavoured pool; scoop it straight from a very cold freezer.

origin.history: Affogato, Italian for 'drowned', is a scoop of gelato with espresso poured over it. It belongs to Italy's twentieth-century espresso-bar culture; no single inventor or date is documented, and it became widely known outside Italy only from the late twentieth century.
